Found it — the lookup does an exact-case match against the orderId, so a lowercase input like "a-1001" fails silently and gets treated as not found. I should fix this in tools.ts since that's where the lookup happens and it covers both orderStatus and orderAgent, normalizing the orderId with trim and uppercase before comparing. I'm also noting that createRefund uses the same ORDERS record, so I need to check whether this fix needs to apply there too.

I'll verify quickly by checking the orders.json data directly rather than guessing. The actual fix belongs in tools.ts, though createRefund in db.ts has the same case-sensitivity flaw and would fail similarly—worth noting as a related gap even if out of scope. For the fix itself, I'll normalize the orderId with both uppercase conversion and trimming, since whitespace from copy-pasted input is just as plausible a cause as case mismatch.

Type-check is clean (only npm update notices in the output). Now I'll write `answer.json` with the broken line exactly as it was before the edit.

The root cause is in `src/tools.ts`: `lookupOrder` does an exact, case-sensitive key lookup, so a lowercase id like `a-1001` returns `null` and the model reports the order as not found. I fixed it by normalizing the id before the lookup, `ORDERS[orderId.trim().toUpperCase()]`. Running the lookup against `orders.json` confirms `a-1001` now resolves to the same record as `A-1001`, and the TypeScript check is clean. I wrote `answer.json` in the project root with the broken line, cause and evidence.

I did not run the Genkit flow end to end, since that needs the model API. The trim is a small addition beyond the reported case issue, for pasted ids with stray spaces.

`createRefund` in `src/db.ts` (line 26) has the same case-sensitive lookup, so `refundAgent` will still fail on a lowercase id. I left it alone because it wasn't part of this report, but it's a one-line change if you want it.
